predecessors.name: House of Khalifa
predecessors.text: the Qatar peninsula, which the Al Khalifa 'claimed ... by 1783' and over which they 'continued to exert authority over the mainland'

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Qatar, incorporated by January 1872 as a province in Najd under the sanjak of Najd, with Jassim bin Mohammed as kaymakam

ledger.x: 1847: the Al Khalifa attack the Qatari coast.
1851: Najd occupies Qatar for a month.

1851: the Qatari-Bahraini conflict of 1847-1851 ends with the peace of 25 July 1851 brokered by Saeed bin Tahnun, which returned Al Bidda to Ali bin Khalifa's chieftainship (History of Qatar page); Mohammed bin Thani relinquished his position.

wars.name: Qatari-Bahraini conflicts of 1847-1851
wars.outcome: The Al Khalifa won at Fuwayrit and razed Al Bidda (17 November 1847); Faisal's Najd took Qatar for a month after the Battle of Mesaimeer (June 1851) and made peace on 25 July.

wars.name: Qatari-Bahraini War
wars.outcome: Al Wakrah and Al Bidda were sacked in 1867; the Battle of Damsah (late 1867 or June 1868) killed about 1,000; Pelly's 1868 settlement acknowledged Mohammed bin Thani.

wars.name: Ottoman incorporation of Qatar
wars.outcome: No fighting: 100 Ottoman troops landed at Al Bidda in December 1871 at Jassim bin Mohammed's invitation and Qatar became a province in Najd by January 1872.

certainty.note: The peninsula had no recognised boundary before the 1916 treaty (the History of Qatar page names only the Zubarah and Hawar disputes and a 1922 Uqair line); the coast and towns are the only certain land.
